chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya al-Azraq from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman who performed the Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) from Umrah to Hajj, and she completed the Umrah Tawaf and feared menstruation before the Day of Nahr (sacrifice). Is it permissible for her to hasten her Tawaf by performing the Tawaf of Hajj before going to Mina? He said: 'If she fears being compelled to do so, she should do it.'

And if the woman is weak/ill, there is no harm if she is carried around (for Tawaf). And if there is crowding at the Stone (al-Hajar), there is no harm if she leaves the Istilam (kissing/touching the Stone). And if she is carried until she touches it, that is better. Narrated.

key_terms.الاسْتِلَامَ: Istilam (touching/kissing the Black Stone or corner)
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ: Day of Nahr (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the concessions for a woman fearing menstruation during Hajj regarding Tawaf and Istilam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *darura* (necessity) in Hajj jurisprudence, allowing a woman performing Tamattu' to merge her Umrah Tawaf with Hajj Tawaf if she fears menstruation will prevent her from performing Tawaf al-Qudum in Mina. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in ritual worship, extending similar concessions to the ill or weak regarding physical exertion and the specific act of Istilam during crowded conditions. It underscores the flexibility within the strictures of Hajj to accommodate natural biological realities and physical limitations.
